reasoning_traces.think:
The Pose2Trajectory system integrates multi-modal sensory inputs—player pose, ball position, and temporal context—into a unified encoder-decoder framework. It leverages Time2Vec to embed temporal structure, enabling the model to reason about motion evolution over time. The LSTM post-processing step ensures smoothness in camera tracking signals, crucial for broadcast automation. The core innovation lies in combining spatial (joint positions) and temporal (Time2Vec) features to predict image-plane centroids. However, the model's reliance on pixel-space metrics and its domain-specific design (tennis) limits generalizability. Its failure mode occurs when pose estimation fails or ball tracking is lost, leading to inaccurate predictions. The system assumes that image-plane centroids are sufficient for camera automation, which may not hold under complex scenes or varying camera angles. The lack of external baselines and train-test leakage risks further undermine confidence in empirical claims.
